source.title: Limiting shape for directed percolation models

results.label: Proposition 2.1
results.title: Directional passage-time limits
results.summary: Establishes the deterministic directional shape from almost-sure passage-time limits. It also proves convergence in mean when the limit is finite, scaling under multiplication of the direction, invariance under coordinate permutations, and superadditivity.
definitions: Superadditivity means $g(x+y)\ge g(x)+g(y)$. The common notation page defines the directional shape $g$.
results.notes: The guide defines $g$ by the almost-sure directional limit. It separately records the problem with the paper's off-lattice supremum formula (2.3) for signed weights. Uniform convergence over many directions is not part of this proposition.

coverage.scope: All four claims hold on $\mathbb R_{\ge0}^2$ with the same finite-first-moment hypothesis, allowing $g(x)=+\infty$. Directions in $\mathbb R_{\ge0}^d$ for $d\ge3$ are outside this certificate.

restriction.label: Planar case only
restriction.paper_scope: For every integer $d\ge2$, all four directional-limit and shape-property claims assume $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$.
restriction.certified_scope: All four claims hold on $\mathbb R_{\ge0}^2$ with the same finite-first-moment hypothesis, allowing $g(x)=+\infty$.
restriction.gap: Directions in $\mathbb R_{\ge0}^d$ for $d\ge3$ are outside this certificate.
restriction.reason: The released model uses the lattice $\mathbb Z^2$ and two-coordinate directions. Its certificates have no dimension parameter. The limitation is the omission of higher dimensions; all planar cases under the paper’s assumptions are covered.
restriction.impact: Every planar conclusion is covered. Finiteness and continuity under further assumptions are separate certified results; they are not assumed in this proposition.

results.label: Proposition 2.2
results.title: Finite values of the shape
results.summary: Gives a sufficient condition for the directional shape to take finite values in every direction. The condition controls large positive weights; the negative part needs only the first moment already used to define the shape.
definitions: For the weight law $\mu$, write $I_+^{(d)}(\mu)=\int_0^\infty\mathbb P\{\omega_0>t\}^{1/d}\,dt$. At $d=2$ this is the positive square-root-tail integral.

coverage.scope: Finiteness in every planar direction is certified under $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$ and $I_+^{(2)}(\mu)<\infty$. The corresponding $d\ge3$ finiteness result is outside this certificate.

restriction.label: Planar case only
restriction.paper_scope: For every $d\ge2$, finiteness of the directional shape follows from $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$ and $I_+^{(d)}(\mu)<\infty$.
restriction.certified_scope: Finiteness in every planar direction is certified under $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$ and $I_+^{(2)}(\mu)<\infty$.
restriction.gap: The corresponding $d\ge3$ finiteness result is outside this certificate.
restriction.reason: The released model uses the lattice $\mathbb Z^2$ and two-coordinate directions. Its certificates have no dimension parameter. The limitation is the omission of higher dimensions; all planar cases under the paper’s assumptions are covered.
restriction.impact: The full planar finiteness conclusion used in Theorem 2.3 is covered. No stronger planar moment condition is imposed.

results.label: Theorem 2.3
results.title: Continuity at boundary points
results.summary: Proves that the directional shape is continuous throughout its domain, including the coordinate axes. Thus approaching an axis from the interior gives the same limiting value as the directional limit defined directly on that axis.
definitions: For the weight law $\mu$, write $I_+^{(d)}(\mu)=\int_0^\infty\mathbb P\{\omega_0>t\}^{1/d}\,dt$. At $d=2$ this is the positive square-root-tail integral.

coverage.scope: Continuity on all of $\mathbb R_{\ge0}^2$, including both axes and the origin, under $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$ and $I_+^{(2)}(\mu)<\infty$. Continuity in dimensions $d\ge3$ is outside this certificate.

restriction.label: Planar case only
restriction.paper_scope: Continuity throughout $\mathbb R_{\ge0}^d$ for every $d\ge2$, assuming $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$ and $I_+^{(d)}(\mu)<\infty$.
restriction.certified_scope: Continuity on all of $\mathbb R_{\ge0}^2$, including both axes and the origin, under $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$ and $I_+^{(2)}(\mu)<\infty$.
restriction.gap: Continuity in dimensions $d\ge3$ is outside this certificate.
restriction.reason: The released model uses the lattice $\mathbb Z^2$ and two-coordinate directions. Its certificates have no dimension parameter. The limitation is the omission of higher dimensions; all planar cases under the paper’s assumptions are covered.
restriction.impact: The planar main theorem is covered in full, including boundary continuity.

results.label: Theorem 2.4
results.title: Shape near a coordinate axis
results.summary: Identifies the leading change in the planar last-passage shape near a coordinate axis. Its first correction is determined by the weight variance and has square-root order, with a smaller remainder under the stated tail assumptions.

coverage.scope: The full conclusion of Theorem 2.4 is certified.

results.label: Corollary 2.5(i)
results.title: A finite continuous first-passage shape
results.summary: Transfers finiteness and continuity to the first-passage shape by changing the signs of the weights. Here first passage means minimizing, rather than maximizing, the weight of a directed path between the same endpoints.
definitions: For the weight law $\mu$, write $I_-^{(d)}(\mu)=\int_{-\infty}^0\mathbb P\{\omega_0\le t\}^{1/d}\,dt$. At $d=2$ this is the negative square-root-tail integral.

coverage.scope: The same conclusions hold on $\mathbb R_{\ge0}^2$ under $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$ and $I_-^{(2)}(\mu)<\infty$. The $d\ge3$ cases are outside this certificate.

restriction.label: Planar case only
restriction.paper_scope: Finiteness and continuity of the first-passage shape on $\mathbb R_{\ge0}^d$ for every $d\ge2$, assuming $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$ and $I_-^{(d)}(\mu)<\infty$.
restriction.certified_scope: The same conclusions hold on $\mathbb R_{\ge0}^2$ under $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$ and $I_-^{(2)}(\mu)<\infty$.
restriction.gap: The $d\ge3$ cases are outside this certificate.
restriction.reason: The released model uses the lattice $\mathbb Z^2$ and two-coordinate directions. Its certificates have no dimension parameter. The limitation is the omission of higher dimensions; all planar cases under the paper’s assumptions are covered.
restriction.impact: The planar corollary is covered in full. The certificate uses expected passage-time limits; Proposition 2.1 applied to negated weights identifies the same directional almost-sure shape. This is a change of presentation, not a lost conclusion.

results.label: Corollary 2.5(ii)
results.title: First-passage shape near an axis
results.summary: Gives the corresponding square-root correction for the planar first-passage shape near an axis. The correction has the opposite sign from last passage, while its size is again determined by the weight variance.

coverage.scope: The full conclusion of Corollary 2.5(ii) is certified.

results.label: Lemma 3.1
results.title: A probability bound for a maximum of sums
results.summary: Controls the probability that a maximum of sums differs from its expectation. The random variables are independent and bounded, and every permitted sum uses only a bounded number of them; the estimate applies beyond percolation.

coverage.scope: The full conclusion of Lemma 3.1 is certified.

results.label: Lemma 3.2
results.title: Changing a small coordinate
results.summary: For bounded weights, adding a sufficiently small missing coordinate changes the shape by a small amount. One choice of how small works uniformly over all starting points on a bounded part of the coordinate face.
definitions: A coordinate face consists of points in $\mathbb R_{\ge0}^d$ at which one specified coordinate is zero.

coverage.scope: The full uniform conclusion holds near both planar axes under the same bounded-weight assumption $\mathbb P\{|\omega_0|\le b\}=1$ for some finite $b$. Coordinate faces in dimensions $d\ge3$ are outside the certificate.

restriction.label: Planar case only
restriction.paper_scope: For bounded weights in every $d\ge2$, one neighborhood size works uniformly near any coordinate face within a prescribed bounded region.
restriction.certified_scope: The full uniform conclusion holds near both planar axes under the same bounded-weight assumption $\mathbb P\{|\omega_0|\le b\}=1$ for some finite $b$.
restriction.gap: Coordinate faces in dimensions $d\ge3$ are outside the certificate.
restriction.reason: The released model uses the lattice $\mathbb Z^2$ and two-coordinate directions. Its certificates have no dimension parameter. The limitation is the omission of higher dimensions; all planar cases under the paper’s assumptions are covered.
restriction.impact: Both axis estimates needed for the planar continuity proof are covered. There is no unproved planar boundary case.

results.label: Lemma 3.3
results.title: Continuity for bounded weights
results.summary: Proves continuity of the shape throughout its closed nonnegative domain when the weights lie in a fixed bounded interval. Boundary directions are included.
definitions: A coordinate face consists of points in $\mathbb R_{\ge0}^d$ at which one specified coordinate is zero.

coverage.scope: Continuity on all of $\mathbb R_{\ge0}^2$ for every law satisfying $\mathbb P\{|\omega_0|\le b\}=1$ for some finite $b$. Continuity in dimensions $d\ge3$ is outside this certificate.

restriction.label: Planar case only
restriction.paper_scope: For bounded weights, continuity on $\mathbb R_{\ge0}^d$ for every $d\ge2$.
restriction.certified_scope: Continuity on all of $\mathbb R_{\ge0}^2$ for every law satisfying $\mathbb P\{|\omega_0|\le b\}=1$ for some finite $b$.
restriction.gap: Continuity in dimensions $d\ge3$ is outside this certificate.
restriction.reason: The released model uses the lattice $\mathbb Z^2$ and two-coordinate directions. Its certificates have no dimension parameter. The limitation is the omission of higher dimensions; all planar cases under the paper’s assumptions are covered.
restriction.impact: The entire bounded-weight planar statement is covered and supplies the planar truncation argument.

results.label: Proposition 3.4
results.title: Weight bounds for connected sets
results.summary: Bounds the largest total weight of a connected set containing the origin, both in expectation and almost surely after division by the set size. A constant depending only on dimension controls every weight law satisfying the positive-tail condition.
definitions: For the weight law $\mu$, write $I_+^{(d)}(\mu)=\int_0^\infty\mathbb P\{\omega_0>t\}^{1/d}\,dt$. At $d=2$ this is the positive square-root-tail integral.
The positive part is $\omega_z^+=\max\{\omega_z,0\}$. Connected sets use lattice edges joining vertices that differ by one in exactly one coordinate.

coverage.scope: Both bounds are covered on $\mathbb Z^2$ under $I_+^{(2)}(\mu)<\infty$, with a constant independent of the law and set size. The expectation certificate bounds the larger maximum obtained from positive-part weights, so it also bounds the signed maximum. The bounds for connected sets in $\mathbb Z^d$ with $d\ge3$ are outside these certificates.

restriction.label: Planar case only
restriction.paper_scope: Expected and almost-sure upper bounds for the maximum total weight of connected sets of a given size containing the origin in $\mathbb Z^d$, for every $d\ge2$, under $I_+^{(d)}(\mu)<\infty$.
restriction.certified_scope: Both bounds are covered on $\mathbb Z^2$ under $I_+^{(2)}(\mu)<\infty$, with a constant independent of the law and set size. The expectation certificate bounds the larger maximum obtained from positive-part weights, so it also bounds the signed maximum.
restriction.gap: The bounds for connected sets in $\mathbb Z^d$ with $d\ge3$ are outside these certificates.
restriction.reason: The released model uses the lattice $\mathbb Z^2$ and two-coordinate directions. Its certificates have no dimension parameter. The limitation is the omission of higher dimensions; all planar cases under the paper’s assumptions are covered.
restriction.impact: The complete planar upper estimates are available. No negative-tail moment is added by replacing weights by their positive parts for an upper bound.

results.label: Lemma 3.5
results.title: Upper and lower passage bounds
results.summary: Converts the connected-set bounds into upper bounds for directed passage times and the shape. It also bounds the shape below by the path length times the mean weight, keeping the positive-tail and first-moment assumptions distinct.
definitions: For the weight law $\mu$, write $I_+^{(d)}(\mu)=\int_0^\infty\mathbb P\{\omega_0>t\}^{1/d}\,dt$. At $d=2$ this is the positive square-root-tail integral.

coverage.scope: The planar upper bounds and both planar shape bounds are covered. The mean lower bound uses only $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$; the upper bounds use $I_+^{(2)}(\mu)<\infty$. The $d\ge3$ versions are outside the linked certificates.

links.label: Mean lower bound under a first moment

restriction.label: Planar case only
restriction.paper_scope: For every $d\ge2$, expected and almost-sure passage upper bounds under $I_+^{(d)}(\mu)<\infty$, and the stated shape bounds with the finite first moment used to define $g$.
restriction.certified_scope: The planar upper bounds and both planar shape bounds are covered. The mean lower bound uses only $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$; the upper bounds use $I_+^{(2)}(\mu)<\infty$.
restriction.gap: The $d\ge3$ versions are outside the linked certificates.
restriction.reason: The released model uses the lattice $\mathbb Z^2$ and two-coordinate directions. Its certificates have no dimension parameter. The limitation is the omission of higher dimensions; all planar cases under the paper’s assumptions are covered.
restriction.impact: Every planar bound used by the main theorems is covered. The released first-moment lower-bound proof avoids the extra negative moment present in a different standalone helper.

results.label: Lemma 3.6
results.title: Effect of capping large weights
results.summary: Quantifies how the shape changes when weights outside a bounded interval are moved to its endpoints. Separate errors account for the lower and upper tails, and both vanish uniformly over bounded sets of directions as the interval expands.
definitions: For the weight law $\mu$, write $I_+^{(d)}(\mu)=\int_0^\infty\mathbb P\{\omega_0>t\}^{1/d}\,dt$. At $d=2$ this is the positive square-root-tail integral.
results.notes: This compares deterministic shape functions as the weight cutoff grows. It is different from convergence of random passage times as the distance grows.

coverage.scope: Both comparisons and the full uniform approximation on bounded subsets of $\mathbb R_{\ge0}^2$ hold under $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$ and $I_+^{(2)}(\mu)<\infty$. Directions in dimensions $d\ge3$ are outside these certificates.

restriction.label: Planar case only
restriction.paper_scope: In every $d\ge2$, the two shape comparisons and convergence uniform on bounded direction sets assume $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$ and $I_+^{(d)}(\mu)<\infty$.
restriction.certified_scope: Both comparisons and the full uniform approximation on bounded subsets of $\mathbb R_{\ge0}^2$ hold under $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$ and $I_+^{(2)}(\mu)<\infty$.
restriction.gap: Directions in dimensions $d\ge3$ are outside these certificates.
restriction.reason: The released model uses the lattice $\mathbb Z^2$ and two-coordinate directions. Its certificates have no dimension parameter. The limitation is the omission of higher dimensions; all planar cases under the paper’s assumptions are covered.
restriction.impact: The complete planar truncation comparison is covered, including signed unbounded weights under the stated conditions.

results.label: Lemma 4.1
results.title: A bound for Bernoulli weights
results.summary: Gives an explicit upper bound on the planar shape for weights that are either zero or one. The bound separates the mean contribution from a square-root correction and supplies the estimate used to compare general weight distributions.

coverage.scope: The full conclusion of Lemma 4.1 is certified.

results.label: Lemma 4.2
results.title: Changing the weight distribution
results.summary: Bounds the difference between two planar shapes after subtracting the contribution of their different mean weights. The remaining error is controlled by an integral comparing their distribution functions and becomes smaller near a coordinate axis.

coverage.scope: The full conclusion of Lemma 4.2 is certified.

results.label: Lemma 4.3
results.title: Bounded weights with the same mean and variance
results.summary: Approximates an unbounded weight law by bounded laws while preserving its mean and variance exactly. Closeness is measured by integrating the square root of the difference between distribution functions, so the shape comparison can be applied.
definitions: A bounded law assigns probability one to some finite interval.

coverage.scope: The full conclusion of Lemma 4.3 is certified.

results.label: Lemma 4.4
results.title: Grouping consecutive weights
results.summary: Compares the original shape with the shape obtained by summing weights in horizontal groups. As the direction approaches an axis, suitable increasing group sizes make the rescaled shape error smaller than the square-root correction of interest.
definitions: For a group of size $r$, its weight law is that of the sum of $r$ independent original weights.

coverage.scope: The full conclusion of Lemma 4.4 is certified.

results.label: Lemma 4.5
results.title: Comparing grouped weights with normal weights
results.summary: For bounded weights, compares the shape of large sums with the shape for normal weights. After adjusting for the original mean and variance, the error is smaller than the square-root correction near the axis.
definitions: Normal comparison weights have mean zero and variance one before the stated mean and variance adjustments.

coverage.scope: The full conclusion of Lemma 4.5 is certified.

results.label: Lemma 4.6
results.title: A normal comparison near the axis
results.summary: Extends the normal comparison from bounded weights to all laws satisfying the paper's two tail conditions. This isolates the mean and variance as the distribution-dependent quantities in the leading near-axis behavior of the shape.
definitions: Normal comparison weights have mean zero and variance one before adjustment to the original mean and variance.

coverage.scope: The full conclusion of Lemma 4.6 is certified.

results.label: Theorem 5.1
results.title: Passage-time level sets at large times
results.summary: Turns uniform passage-time approximation into almost-sure convergence of rescaled passage-time level sets. Last passage requires a positive mean; first passage requires a uniform positive linear lower bound on its directional shape.
definitions: Write $I_+^{(d)}(\mu)=\int_0^\infty\mathbb P\{\omega_0>t\}^{1/d}\,dt$ and $I_-^{(d)}(\mu)=\int_{-\infty}^0\mathbb P\{\omega_0\le t\}^{1/d}\,dt$. Here $\mu$ is the common weight law.
results.notes: The displayed set inclusions are written in the usual range $0<\varepsilon<1$ so that both dilation factors are nonnegative. The first-passage positive lower bound is an additional premise, not a property that follows from the tail assumptions alone.

coverage.scope: Both growth-set conclusions hold in dimension two under the same tail and positivity assumptions. The growth-set conclusions in dimensions $d\ge3$ are outside the certificates.

restriction.label: Planar case only
restriction.paper_scope: For every $d\ge2$, last- and first-passage growth-set convergence under $I_+^{(d)}(\mu),I_-^{(d)}(\mu)<\infty$. Last passage also assumes $m=\mathbb E\omega_0>0$; first passage assumes $h(x)\ge c\sum_i x_i$ for all nonnegative $x$, with some $c>0$.
restriction.certified_scope: Both growth-set conclusions hold in dimension two under the same tail and positivity assumptions.
restriction.gap: The growth-set conclusions in dimensions $d\ge3$ are outside the certificates.
restriction.reason: The released model uses the lattice $\mathbb Z^2$ and two-coordinate directions. Its certificates have no dimension parameter. The limitation is the omission of higher dimensions; all planar cases under the paper’s assumptions are covered.
restriction.impact: Both planar main growth theorems are covered. The positive linear lower bound for first passage remains a premise, exactly as in the paper; it is not silently derived from the tail assumptions.

results.label: Remark 5.1(i)
results.title: Checking a positive lower bound
results.summary: Reduces a uniform positive lower bound for the first-passage shape to positivity in the diagonal direction. The remark also gives a sufficient condition using directed percolation when weights are nonnegative; the linked certificate covers only the deterministic inequality.
definitions: Here $h:\mathbb R_{\ge0}^2\to\mathbb R$ satisfies $h(cx)=ch(x)$ for $c\ge0$, $h(x_2,x_1)=h(x_1,x_2)$ and $h(x+y)\le h(x)+h(y)$.
For nonnegative weights, $\mu(\{0\})$ is the probability of a zero-weight site. The number $p_c^{(d)}$ is the critical probability for an infinite directed open-site path in dimension $d$.

coverage.scope: For $x\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^2$, the certificate proves $h(x)\ge(x_1+x_2)h(1,1)/2$ from homogeneity, coordinate symmetry and subadditivity. Hence $h(1,1)>0$ gives the required planar linear lower bound. The linked proof does not establish the inequality for $d\ge3$ or derive $h(1,1)>0$ from the zero-weight probability. The latter is a separate probabilistic assertion, rather than an assumption of the deterministic inequality.

restriction.label: Planar inequality only
restriction.paper_scope: In every dimension $d\ge2$, the diagonal value determines whether $h$ has a positive linear lower bound. For nonnegative weights, the paper also asserts that $\mu(\{0\})<p_c^{(d)}$ guarantees this positivity.
restriction.certified_scope: For $x\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^2$, the certificate proves $h(x)\ge(x_1+x_2)h(1,1)/2$ from homogeneity, coordinate symmetry and subadditivity. Hence $h(1,1)>0$ gives the required planar linear lower bound.
restriction.gap: The linked proof does not establish the inequality for $d\ge3$ or derive $h(1,1)>0$ from the zero-weight probability. The latter is a separate probabilistic assertion, rather than an assumption of the deterministic inequality.
restriction.reason: The proof combines the two coordinates of an arbitrary deterministic function. It neither constructs a percolation model nor relates its critical probability to the first-passage shape.
restriction.impact: The certified planar first-passage growth theorem still applies when its positive linear lower bound is supplied. This entry does not justify replacing that premise by the zero-weight criterion. The planar last-passage and differentiability theorems are unaffected.

results.label: Remark 5.1(ii)
results.title: Weaker moment assumptions for growth
results.summary: States growth-set conclusions with only a first moment for the negative part in last passage, or the positive part in first passage, retaining the other tail’s integral condition. Released lemmas give both planar conclusions with a moment of some order above one for that part.
definitions: Write $\omega_0^+=\max\{\omega_0,0\}$, $\omega_0^-=\max\{-\omega_0,0\}$, $I_+^{(d)}(\mu)=\int_0^\infty\mathbb P\{\omega_0>t\}^{1/d}\,dt$ and $I_-^{(d)}(\mu)=\int_{-\infty}^0\mathbb P\{\omega_0\le t\}^{1/d}\,dt$.
A positive linear lower bound means $h(x)\ge c\sum_{i=1}^d x_i$ for all $x\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}^d$, with one constant $c>0$.
results.notes: This is a reported extension whose alternative-path proof is not included in the paper. It must not be shown as a consequence of Lemmas 5.2–5.5 under only the weaker moment assumptions.

coverage.scope: The planar last-passage growth conclusion follows from released lemmas under $I_+^{(2)}(\mu)<\infty$, $\mathbb E[(\omega_0^-)^p]<\infty$ for some $p>1$, and a positive mean. Sign change gives the first-passage counterpart under $I_-^{(2)}(\mu)<\infty$, $\mathbb E[(\omega_0^+)^p]<\infty$ for some $p>1$, and the paper's positive linear lower bound for $h$. A finite first moment alone need not give any moment of order $p>1$. Thus the paper's first-moment extensions are not obtained by these proofs; neither are dimensions $d\ge3$. Negating the weights swaps the positive and negative moments, so it does not remove the stronger moment requirement.

links.label: Shape lower bound under the same moments

restriction.label: Planar forms with stronger moments
restriction.paper_scope: For every $d\ge2$, last-passage growth retains $I_+^{(d)}(\mu)<\infty$ but needs only $\mathbb E\omega_0^-<\infty$, together with $\mathbb E\omega_0>0$. First-passage growth retains $I_-^{(d)}(\mu)<\infty$ but needs only $\mathbb E\omega_0^+<\infty$, together with a positive linear lower bound for $h$.
restriction.certified_scope: The planar last-passage growth conclusion follows from released lemmas under $I_+^{(2)}(\mu)<\infty$, $\mathbb E[(\omega_0^-)^p]<\infty$ for some $p>1$, and a positive mean. Sign change gives the first-passage counterpart under $I_-^{(2)}(\mu)<\infty$, $\mathbb E[(\omega_0^+)^p]<\infty$ for some $p>1$, and the paper's positive linear lower bound for $h$.
restriction.gap: A finite first moment alone need not give any moment of order $p>1$. Thus the paper's first-moment extensions are not obtained by these proofs; neither are dimensions $d\ge3$. Negating the weights swaps the positive and negative moments, so it does not remove the stronger moment requirement.
restriction.reason: The uniform lower estimate controls sums of negative weights along grid edges of lengths $2^k$, where $k\ge1$. Its failure-probability bound decays geometrically only when $p>1$, making the sum over all scales finite. At $p=1$ that bound has no decay. This explains the proof's stronger assumption; it does not show the assumption is necessary for the theorem.
restriction.impact: This restriction does not weaken Differentiability of the shape function in the planar corner growth model. That theorem already assumes a negative moment above one, and its positive moment above four gives the positive square-root-tail condition. The standard two-tail planar growth theorem is also covered. The remaining gap is the first-moment generality claimed in this remark.

results.label: Lemma 5.2
results.title: Capping weights changes passage times little
results.summary: Shows that moving weights into a sufficiently large bounded interval changes long passage times by a small fraction of their length. For each chosen interval, the bound holds almost surely for all sufficiently distant lattice endpoints together.
definitions: Write $I_+^{(d)}(\mu)=\int_0^\infty\mathbb P\{\omega_0>t\}^{1/d}\,dt$ and $I_-^{(d)}(\mu)=\int_{-\infty}^0\mathbb P\{\omega_0\le t\}^{1/d}\,dt$. Here $\mu$ is the common weight law.

coverage.scope: The same almost-sure, endpoint-uniform estimate holds on $\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^2$ under $I_+^{(2)}(\mu),I_-^{(2)}(\mu)<\infty$. One deterministic cutoff works before the environment is sampled. The uniform endpoint estimate for $d\ge3$ is outside this certificate.

restriction.label: Planar case only
restriction.paper_scope: For every $d\ge2$, clipping the weights approximates passage times uniformly over all sufficiently distant lattice endpoints under $I_+^{(d)}(\mu),I_-^{(d)}(\mu)<\infty$.
restriction.certified_scope: The same almost-sure, endpoint-uniform estimate holds on $\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^2$ under $I_+^{(2)}(\mu),I_-^{(2)}(\mu)<\infty$. One deterministic cutoff works before the environment is sampled.
restriction.gap: The uniform endpoint estimate for $d\ge3$ is outside this certificate.
restriction.reason: The released model uses the lattice $\mathbb Z^2$ and two-coordinate directions. Its certificates have no dimension parameter. The limitation is the omission of higher dimensions; all planar cases under the paper’s assumptions are covered.
restriction.impact: The complete planar approximation needed by the uniform shape and growth theorems is covered.

results.label: Lemma 5.3
results.title: Capped passage times stay near their means
results.summary: For weights moved into a fixed bounded interval, random passage times differ little from their expectations relative to path length. Almost surely, one distance threshold works for every endpoint, and this holds for every positive error tolerance.

coverage.scope: The same common-event estimate holds over all sufficiently distant endpoints in $\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^2$, for every original probability law. Endpoints in dimensions $d\ge3$ are outside the certificate.

restriction.label: Planar case only
restriction.paper_scope: For every $d\ge2$ and each fixed clipping level, clipped passage times approach their expectations almost surely, uniformly over sufficiently distant endpoints. No moment condition on the original law is assumed.
restriction.certified_scope: The same common-event estimate holds over all sufficiently distant endpoints in $\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^2$, for every original probability law.
restriction.gap: Endpoints in dimensions $d\ge3$ are outside the certificate.
restriction.reason: The released model uses the lattice $\mathbb Z^2$ and two-coordinate directions. Its certificates have no dimension parameter. The limitation is the omission of higher dimensions; all planar cases under the paper’s assumptions are covered.
restriction.impact: The planar statement is covered in full; boundedness comes from clipping, so the original weights need not be bounded or integrable.

results.label: Lemma 5.4
results.title: Mean passage times approach the shape
results.summary: For bounded weights, expected passage times approach the directional shape uniformly over sufficiently distant endpoints. The error is small relative to path length, and the distance threshold is deterministic rather than dependent on the random environment.

coverage.scope: The full deterministic uniform approximation holds on $\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^2$, for every clipped probability law. The uniform expectation estimate for endpoints in $d\ge3$ is outside this certificate.

restriction.label: Planar case only
restriction.paper_scope: For every $d\ge2$ and fixed clipping level, expected clipped passage times approach the clipped shape uniformly over sufficiently distant endpoints.
restriction.certified_scope: The full deterministic uniform approximation holds on $\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^2$, for every clipped probability law.
restriction.gap: The uniform expectation estimate for endpoints in $d\ge3$ is outside this certificate.
restriction.reason: The released model uses the lattice $\mathbb Z^2$ and two-coordinate directions. Its certificates have no dimension parameter. The limitation is the omission of higher dimensions; all planar cases under the paper’s assumptions are covered.
restriction.impact: The entire planar statement is covered. The certificate applies to every bounded law, which includes every clipped law.

results.label: Lemma 5.5
results.title: Capping weights changes the shape little
results.summary: Shows that the shapes for increasingly large bounded weight intervals converge uniformly to the original shape after division by direction length. A single interval size works in every direction.
definitions: Write $I_+^{(d)}(\mu)=\int_0^\infty\mathbb P\{\omega_0>t\}^{1/d}\,dt$ and $I_-^{(d)}(\mu)=\int_{-\infty}^0\mathbb P\{\omega_0\le t\}^{1/d}\,dt$. Here $\mu$ is the common weight law.

coverage.scope: The full relative approximation holds in every planar real direction. It needs only $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$ and $I_+^{(2)}(\mu)<\infty$, which are weaker than the paper's two-tail assumptions. Directions in $d\ge3$ are outside the certificate.

restriction.label: Planar case only
restriction.paper_scope: For every $d\ge2$, the shapes of clipped laws approximate the original shape with error small relative to direction length, under $I_+^{(d)}(\mu),I_-^{(d)}(\mu)<\infty$.
restriction.certified_scope: The full relative approximation holds in every planar real direction. It needs only $\mathbb E|\omega_0|<\infty$ and $I_+^{(2)}(\mu)<\infty$, which are weaker than the paper's two-tail assumptions.
restriction.gap: Directions in $d\ge3$ are outside the certificate.
restriction.reason: The released model uses the lattice $\mathbb Z^2$ and two-coordinate directions. Its certificates have no dimension parameter. The limitation is the omission of higher dimensions; all planar cases under the paper’s assumptions are covered.
restriction.impact: All planar approximation needed by the main proof is covered under at least the paper's assumptions. The non-strict bound gives the printed strict bound at nonzero directions after reducing the tolerance; both shapes are zero at the origin.
